title: The Metal Vault
story: You and NOVA are locked in a metals vault. Its four locks test whether NOVA understands metals and non-metals. NOVA's guesses so far have set off the alarm twice.
escaped: The vault door swings open. NOVA now uses real properties, not looks, and knows rust needs both air and water.

locks.title: Metal or non-metal?
locks.intro: NOVA must sort elements into metals and non-metals. Choose the clues it should use, then test it on gold and iodine.
locks.hint: Iodine is a non-metal, yet it is shiny and greyish. Which property do all the metals share that iodine doesn't?
locks.learn: Looks can fool an AI. Iodine shines like a metal and gold isn't grey. Conducting electricity is a real property of metals, so it sorts both correctly.

locks.title: Check NOVA's chemistry
locks.intro: NOVA explains what happens when metals burn in air. Is it right? Decide and pick the fact that settles it.
locks.claim: When metals burn in oxygen they make acidic oxides.
evidence: Magnesium oxide dissolves in water and turns red litmus blue, so metal oxides are basic.
Metals can be beaten into sheets and drawn into wires.
Sulphur dioxide dissolves in water and turns blue litmus red.
Copper is used to make electric wires.
locks.hint: Sulphur is not a metal. Which fact is about a metal's oxide?
locks.learn: A fact about something similar (sulphur's acidic oxide) can make a wrong claim sound right. The evidence must be about the exact thing claimed: a metal's oxide.

locks.title: Fix NOVA's list of uses
locks.intro: NOVA is learning what metals and non-metals are used for. Tick the examples that are wrong.

rows.label: Electric wires
rows.why: sulphur is a non-metal and doesn't conduct electricity

rows.label: Jewellery that never rusts
rows.why: iron rusts; gold and silver are used for jewellery

locks.hint: Think about which materials conduct electricity and which ones rust.
locks.learn: Some wrong examples break a rule the AI should know (non-metals don't conduct). Catching them before training stops NOVA from learning something impossible.

locks.title: What makes iron rust?
locks.intro: Three iron nails were kept in test tubes for a week. NOVA has the results.
locks.question: NOVA says: 'Water makes iron rust.' What does the data really show?
options: NOVA is right: tube B proves it.
Iron rusted only when it had both air and water (tube C); neither alone was enough.
locks.hint: Tube B had water but didn't rust. Which tube rusted, and what did it have?
locks.learn: An AI must look at all the data, not just the case that fits its idea. Tube B rules out 'water alone'; the pattern is that rusting needs both air (oxygen) and water.
